title: Define rollout plan: feature gate integration + per-model allowlist/denylist + staged region rollout + rollback workflow (kernel auto-selection v2)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Rollout mechanics for kernel auto-selection v2: wire selector enablement into control-plane feature gates, add per-model allowlist/denylist controls (incl. hot reload), define staged region rollout steps for Hosted (then Dedicated pools), and specify a rollback workflow that oncall can execute quickly during tail-latency spikes or correctness concerns.

Primary goals:
- Safe, reversible rollout (fast kill switch; scoped to region/model/GPU where needed).
- Deterministic gate evaluation (same inputs => same decision) and auditable configuration changes.
- Clear ownership/authority during canary windows (who flips gates, who approves rollback).

Non-goals:
- Implementing the selector itself (tracked in ENG-4822/4823 + PRs).
- Dashboard buildout (tracked separately, but rollout must depend on dashboards being usable).
rollout_plan:
Proposed staged rollout (Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private):

1) Pre-canary prerequisites (before any traffic):
- Gate exists in control plane: kernel_selection_v2_enabled.
- Runtime supports evaluating gate + loading allow/deny lists.
- Telemetry emitted for selection decision + gate reason (sampling ok).
- Perf-canary scenario coverage exists for target SKUs and long-context buckets.
- Rollback tested in a staging region with synthetic load.

2) Hosted canary (region staged):
- Stage A: us-east-1, 1% traffic for allowlisted models only.
- Stage B: us-east-1, 10% traffic for allowlisted models; monitor p95/p99 + error rate + selection distribution.
- Stage C: us-east-1, 50% traffic; add 1 additional region (eu-west-1) at 1%.
- Stage D: 100% of allowlisted models across initial regions.
- Expansion: add remaining regions progressively (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%), one region at a time.

3) Dedicated pools:
- Opt-in pilot with 1–2 internal/low-risk Dedicated pools first (known GPU SKUs, stable drivers).
- Customer opt-in by pool: default OFF; allow customers to request enablement via support/onboarding.
- For Dedicated: require explicit model allowlist per pool (avoid surprises with pinned models / special kernels).

4) Private deployments:
- Default OFF.
- Enablement via documented flag + allowlist file; require customer acknowledgement of rollback workflow.
- Provide “force v1” and “force kernel” escape hatches (documented in runbook).

Rollback philosophy:
- Prefer the smallest blast-radius rollback first: disable v2 for a specific (model, gpu_sku, region) combination; fall back to v1 selection.
- If widespread, flip regional kill switch (v2 off for region).
- If systemic, global disable in control-plane + runtime config reload confirmation.

Canary success criteria (minimum):
- No correctness regressions detected by conformance suite.
- p95 latency: no regression > 2% for allowlisted models overall; p99 latency: no regression > 3% (or per SRE guardrail).
- Error rate: no increase > 0.05% absolute attributable to selector changes.
- Selection distribution stable (no unexplained swings in chosen kernels for a given (model, gpu_sku, seq_bucket)).
gate_and_policy_design:
Gate design + evaluation order (deterministic):

Inputs available at request-time:
- model_id (resolved to pinned version where applicable)
- model_family (e.g., llama, mistral, qwen, gemma)
- gpu_sku (normalized: A100-80GB, H100-SXM, L40S, etc.)
- region
- seq_bucket (short/medium/long; prefill/decode regime signal)
- driver/cuda version (if available; otherwise inferred from runtime build tags)

Decision order (first match wins):
1) Hard safety blocks (global): driver/cuda denylist => force v1.
2) Explicit per-model denylist (optionally keyed by gpu_sku and/or region) => force v1.
3) Explicit per-model allowlist (optionally keyed by gpu_sku and/or region) => eligible for v2.
4) Region gate percentage rollout (for eligible set) => v2 for sampled traffic.
5) Default: v1.

Policy constraints:
- Determinism: gate sampling must be stable (e.g., hash(model_id + request_id) with a fixed seed) and documented.
- Auditability: any allow/deny change must be written to control-plane audit logs (who/when/what).
- Hot reload: runtime should pick up policy changes without restart (bounded propagation time target: <5 minutes).
rollback_workflow_definition:
Rollback workflow (operational):

Who can trigger rollback:
- Primary rollback authority during canary: Release Engineering (Connor O’Brien) + SRE oncall (Sean Gallagher / Allison Grant) in consultation with Runtime lead (Hiro Tanaka / Yuki Sato).
- If paging event: SRE can execute emergency rollback immediately and notify Runtime + Release.

How to rollback (in order):
1) Scoped disable: add (model_id, region, gpu_sku) entry to v2 denylist and hot reload.
2) Region kill switch: set kernel_selection_v2_enabled=false for region.
3) Global kill switch: set kernel_selection_v2_enabled=false globally.

Validation steps post-rollback:
- Confirm config propagation (control plane reports effective policy version in each region).
- Confirm telemetry: selection_v2_enabled drops to ~0 for affected slice.
- Confirm latency recovery: p95/p99 returns to baseline within 10–15 minutes (depending on traffic volume).
- Capture incident notes: attach selection traces + exact policy diff applied.

Escalation path:
- If rollback does not recover tail latency, proceed to kernel pinning for the affected model(s) (runtime debug flag / config override) and open incident with Runtime Kernels + Scheduling.
acceptance_criteria: Control-plane feature gate exists for kernel selection v2 and supports region-scoped percentage rollout.
Per-model allowlist/denylist semantics defined, implemented, and documented (including optional gpu_sku and region scoping).
Gate evaluation order is deterministic and recorded in design notes (including sampling approach).
Runtime supports hot reload of policy changes with bounded propagation time; effective policy version exposed in logs/metrics.
Rollback workflow is written, reviewed by SRE + Release Eng, and validated in a staging environment.
Canary plan includes clear success metrics, rollback triggers, and named owners for gate flips and rollback decisions.
comments: 2026-01-10 (Talia Benson): Kicking off ENG-4826. Need a single source of truth for: (a) who flips the gate, (b) how we scope rollout by model, and (c) rollback blast radius controls. Please propose deterministic evaluation order; SRE asked specifically for replayability in incident reviews.

2026-01-14 (Ethan Park): Control-plane can support: global boolean, per-region boolean, per-region percentage rollout (stable hash), and policy bundles with versioning + audit logs. Need exact matching keys for model_id and gpu_sku normalization so we don’t create cardinality bugs / mismatches.

2026-01-17 (Benji Okafor): Draft decision order: hard safety blocks -> denylist -> allowlist -> percentage rollout -> default off. This keeps us safe when we learn new bad combos mid-canary. Will rely on stable sampling via hash(model_id + request_id).

2026-01-21 (Jordan Lee): Determinism note: request_id is not guaranteed stable across retries depending on client. Prefer hash(model_id + trace_id) if present; otherwise fall back to request_id. Also ensure the same input tuple generates the same decision in replay tests.

2026-01-29 (Aisha Bello): Add explicit rollback triggers tied to p99 and error rate. Suggest: rollback if p99 regression > 5% for 10 min in a slice OR if error rate increases >0.1% absolute. Also: require dashboard panels to be live before Stage B (10%).

2026-02-03 (Connor O’Brien): For runtime-1.21 release train, we need a canary window with named gate operator + back-up. Please include ‘who flips the gate’ and ‘who can override’ in the ticket before we move to In Review.

2026-02-07 (Omar El-Sayed): During early testing we saw long-context tail spikes when seq_bucket misclassifies. Rollout plan should keep long-context-heavy models in allowlist only after perf suite verifies. I propose initial allowlist excludes long-context summarization routes until PR-28522 lands.

2026-02-12 (Benji Okafor): Implementing hot reload semantics: policy bundle refresh every 60s, with jitter; max propagation 5 min. Runtime logs effective policy_version on startup and on refresh; metric: selector_policy_version{region,service}.

2026-02-16 (Talia Benson): Marking as In Review once runbook section is reviewed by SRE. Dedicated/Private readiness: please add note that default is OFF for those environments; enablement is opt-in with a pool-level config owner.

2026-02-22 (Allison Grant): SRE sign-off: rollback workflow is actionable; scoping controls sufficient. Please ensure denylist edits are audited and that oncall has a ‘last known good’ policy bundle to revert to. OK to close once PR-28510 merges and rollout checklist references this plan.
2026-02-22 (Benji Okafor): Closed as Done. PR-28460 + PR-28510 merged. Rollout checklist updated to reference decision order + rollback steps. Release Eng confirmed gate operators for canary windows.
final_notes: Outcome: Rollout mechanics standardized for kernel selection v2 (runtime-1.21). Control-plane gate + allow/deny policies provide scoped enablement and fast rollback. Dedicated/Private default OFF with opt-in enablement. SRE-approved rollback triggers and authority model established for canary.
